topics.title: Love Poems and Listener Analysis
topics.summary: Howard reads love poems received in the mail alongside an analysis by listener Jeff, who abruptly quits his construction job to move back to Florida and pursue writing aspirations. Frequent interruptions from callers discuss their own experiences, including a detailed breakdown of show personalities like Gary and Fred Norris.

topics.title: Guests Discuss Radio Accuracy and Notable Guests
topics.summary: During a casual conversation, hosts discuss the accuracy of their radio program with an audience member who guesses at details while reminiscing about past guests like Sam Kinison, Richard Simmons, Joan Rivers, and Eddie Griffin. They also delve into guest ratings – including Pat Cooper’s frequent arguments and Joey & Markey Ramon's chaotic appearances - alongside discussions on Howard Stern memorabilia and the show’s history with recurring figures such as Stuttering John and Billy West.

topics.title: Child Star Discussions and Telethon Concerns
topics.summary: The broadcast features a discussion about former child stars Billy Mummey, Jay North, and Macaulay Culkin. The conversation touches upon concerns regarding the exploitation of young actors like Culkin during telethons, including fundraising efforts for charitable causes and personal struggles faced by these individuals.

topics.title: Tony Orlando’s Unconventional Romance Reflections
topics.summary: During an interview, Tony Orlando recounts a twenty-year relationship that began at eighteen and ended due to his burgeoning success with Dawn. He reflects on watching a friend mature while discussing attraction at youth, ultimately admitting a desire for continued involvement in the entertainment industry despite past depression.

topics.title: Career Instability & Telethon Mishaps
topics.summary: The conversation details a period of instability in the subject’s career, marked by cocaine use, strained relationships with colleagues like Jerry Louis and Howard Stern, and mispronunciation errors during telethons. The hosts discuss personal grievances and self-destructive behavior while analyzing the challenges of public performance.

topics.title: Radio Show Prank and Confusion
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, hosts engage in chaotic conversations about past acquaintances like Sonnyatra and Pat Cooper while attempting to prank two disc jockeys by inserting fabricated commercial breaks. The segment devolves into confusion as the hosts struggle to maintain control of the program amidst bizarre tangents and personal commentary.
